literal: Even if I look at her having been thinking of her, she gets angry saying, 'With that much intensity, whom did you think of and look at me?'
translation: Even when I gaze at her after thinking of her with deep affection, she gets angry and demands, 'Whom were you thinking of, to look at me with such intense passion?'
modern: நான் அவளையே நினைத்துக் கொண்டு அவளைப் பார்த்தாலும், 'நீர் யாரை நினைத்துக் கொண்டு என்னை இப்படிப் பார்க்கிறீர்?' என்று சொல்லி அவள் கோபித்துக் கொள்கிறாள்.
explanation: This couplet depicts a subtle lover's tiff where the heroine finds a reason to be angry even in her lover's affectionate gaze. The hero has been thinking of her constantly, and when he looks at her with that deep, lingering love, she misinterprets his intense look. She asks him, 'Whom were you thinking of just now, that you look at me with such a look?' The word 'அனைத்து' refers to the intensity or manner of his gaze, and 'உள்ளி' means remembering or thinking of someone. Her feigned anger shows the playful, delicate nature of their love.
